analysis.investment_thesis: Meesho is a loss-deepening e-commerce marketplace trading at 50x book value with no earnings power, competing in one of the world's most brutal retail wars against Amazon and Flipkart. I don't buy businesses that lose money at scale and carry no durable advantage — this is speculation, not investing.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at solid 28% CAGR (₹5,735→₹9,390 Cr), showing genuine top-line traction in Tier 2/3 India
92% gross margin confirms a pure marketplace/asset-light model — no inventory risk
Operating cash flow turned positive (₹539 Cr in FY25) and near-zero debt (D/E 0.09) limits bankruptcy risk
key_risks: Net loss catastrophically widened to ₹3,942 Cr in FY25 from ₹328 Cr in FY24 — losses accelerating, not converging
No economic moat: price-sensitive social commerce is easily replicated; Amazon, Flipkart, and Reliance have far deeper pockets
P/B of 50x with negative ROE (-264%) and eroding equity base (₹2,472→₹1,446 Cr) means you're paying extraordinary prices for a deteriorating book
red_flags: Net loss exploded 12x in one year (FY24: -₹328 Cr → FY25: -₹3,942 Cr) — something seriously wrong operationally or in 'Other Income' (-₹835 Cr swing)
Promoter holding is only 16.57% — insiders have minimal skin in the game for a founder-led startup narrative
Investing CF of -₹2,638 Cr in FY25 with no clear explanation of asset deployment; total assets jumped ₹3,065 Cr in one year
Forward P/E of -322x and EV/EBITDA of -44x — no valuation framework supports buying at this price
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Meesho is exactly the kind of business I've avoided my entire career: a money-losing internet marketplace priced as though it has already won a war it hasn't even begun to win. The FY25 numbers are alarming — net losses ballooned from ₹328 Cr to ₹3,942 Cr even as revenue grew 23%, and EBITDA swung from -₹281 Cr to -₹1,002 Cr. The 92% gross margin is structurally attractive (pure platform take-rate), but all that gross profit evaporates into sales, marketing, and tech costs. Operating CF turning positive (₹539 Cr) is the one genuine bright spot, but it's overwhelmed by ₹2,638 Cr in investing outflows — and nobody has clearly explained where that capital went.

At ₹74,700 Cr market cap on ₹9,390 Cr revenue (P/S of 6.5x) with deeply negative earnings, the market is pricing in a future of dominant profitability that I see no evidence will materialize. Indian e-commerce is structurally low-margin, ferociously competitive, and Meesho's wedge — unbranded goods for value-conscious Tier 2/3 shoppers — is easily contested by Reliance's JioMart, Flipkart, and dozens of well-funded challengers. There is no pricing power, no switching cost, and no network effect strong enough to justify a 50x price-to-book on negative equity returns. I would not touch this at any price close to current levels.
